clue.text: No rating review is unenlightened

indicators.note: to review is to look over again and rework, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a show given no stars must have come from an ill-informed critic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' is the anagram signal: the eight letters of NO RATING are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninformed, lacking knowledge, is unenlightened.

clue.text: And so on from Rome

parts.note: the Latin expression, as the Romans would say it, for 'and the rest' or 'and so on'

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for 'and the rest' is used in English to mean 'and so on'.

clue.text: Support at the front requires true martial virtue

indicators.note: the support piece is placed first, at the front of the answer

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
very can mean true or real, as in 'the very man'

explanation.surface: Backing those in the front line demands real soldierly courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage is the chief virtue of a soldier.

clue.text: Hothead infuriated over European farming strategy

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: mad means angry, infuriated
CAP is the EU's Common Agricultural Policy

explanation.surface: An angry farmer rages about Brussels agricultural policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is a reckless, impulsive person, a hothead.

clue.text: A grinding job makes him sicker by the minute

indicators.note: by means beside, so the one piece stands next to the other

parts.note: iller means more unwell, sicker

explanation.surface: Monotonous work makes someone feel worse with every passing minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who grinds corn at a mill has that trade.

clue.text: I, serving a meat stew? Anything but!

definitions.text: I, serving a meat stew? Anything but!

indicators.note: a stew is a jumble of ingredients mixed together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A guest is aghast at being offered a meat stew, insisting on anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' signals an anagram of I SERVING A MEAT; the whole clue then describes the attitude of a person who refuses meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of not eating meat makes a meat stew the last thing one would accept.

clue.text: Band of thugs no one can escape from

definitions.text: Band of thugs no one can escape from

parts.words: Band of thugs no one can escape from
parts.note: read as a violent ring of thugs, but really a nasty chain of cause and effect that keeps feeding itself

explanation.definitionFit: A situation where each problem causes another that worsens the first, trapping those inside it.

clue.text: Lost the opportunity for an overseas trip

definitions.meaning: failed to take a chance while it was there
literally, arrived too late for the ship sailing abroad

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for letting a chance slip, taken literally, is failing to catch the ship sailing abroad.

clue.text: The first piece legislation in play

definitions.text: The first piece legislation in play

parts.words: The first piece legislation in play
parts.note: a play's opening division, read cryptically as a statute (act) numbered first among a theatrical piece's laws

explanation.definitionFit: The opening section of a stage play is its first act.

clue.text: He makes notes of a case with a catalogue attached

parts.note: VOC is the abbreviation for the vocative case in grammar
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: A clerk takes notes on a legal case, attaching an inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: The vocative is the grammatical case used for addressing someone, abbreviated VOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer produces musical notes.

clue.text: Wrap up an indecisive contest

definitions.meaning: to bind or fasten something, as with string
a game ending level, with no winner

explanation.definitionFit: To bind with string is to fasten; a drawn match ends level.

clue.text: Silver displayed in the house merits due deference

indicators.note: the silver is shown inside the house, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a house is a home
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Family silverware on show in a stately house earns proper respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is public honour or respect shown to someone.

clue.text: One writing articles about ale

parts.note: re means about or concerning
porter is a dark beer, a type of ale

explanation.surface: A journalist pens pieces about beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist writes newspaper articles.

clue.text: Men about to catch a whale

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Sailors are poised to harpoon a whale.
explanation.definitionFit: An orc is a killer whale, or a similar sea creature.

clue.text: Butter on a wooden plate

parts.note: ash is a type of wood
a tray is a flat plate for carrying things

explanation.surface: A knob of butter served on a wooden platter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is read as 'butt-er', the thing that takes cigarette butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle for cigarette ends takes the butts, so is jokingly a butt-holder.

clue.text: Over the hill? Nonsense!

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for a hill is read backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone protests indignantly at being called past it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the hill' looks like a phrase for old age, but 'Over' is the reversal signal applied to TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is rubbish talk, nonsense.

clue.text: Brogues worth a dollar

parts.note: a dollar is worth a hundred, C, cents

explanation.surface: A pair of shoes costing a single dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, and a dollar is a hundred cents; 'worth' links the two. A brogue is an Irish accent, not only a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional, especially Irish, manner of speech.

clue.text: Giving offence by changing sides

definitions.meaning: annoying or thwarting someone, as in going against them
going over to the opposite side, as across a road or floor

explanation.definitionFit: Opposing someone angers them; going over to the other side is a traverse.

clue.text: Quality controller who used to work at the coal-face

definitions.meaning: an inspector who tests and checks things

definitions.text: who used to work at the coal-face

explanation.definitionFit: An inspector checks quality; split as ex-a-miner it is a former pitman.

clue.text: There has developed an Islamic centre

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somewhere a new place of Muslim learning has grown up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran, the capital of Iran, is a major city of the Muslim world.

clue.text: Wrongly report an art gallery beauty queen!

parts.note: beauty contest winners are titled Miss, as in Miss World
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A newspaper misidentifies a beauty pageant winner as a gallery painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To misstate is to give a false account of something.

clue.text: Hare-brained Tom's in the pigpen

indicators.note: the cat is in the sty, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
a tom is a male cat; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Only a scatterbrained cat would wander into a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty means dizzy and absent-minded, flighty.

clue.text: Copper and gold put into the fire

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
to burn something is to put it into the fire

explanation.surface: Metals are thrown into a furnace to be smelted.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper here is a reddish-brown colour, the shade of auburn hair.

clue.text: Approved of Catherine's entry in the dictionary

indicators.note: the name enters the dictionary, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
Kay is a short form of the name Catherine

explanation.surface: Catherine's definition has been accepted for the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the OK is to sanction or approve.

clue.text: The man's hiding in North Islington

indicators.note: the word is concealed inside the run of clue letters that follows

explanation.surface: A man is lying low in a north London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a borough of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive belonging to a male person.

clue.text: Rush or saunter to the Senior Common Room

parts.note: SCR is the abbreviation for a university's Senior Common Room
to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace, saunter

explanation.surface: A don wonders whether to hurry or stroll over to the staff lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: A Senior Common Room is the lounge for academic staff at a British university.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble is to hurry in a disorderly way, to rush.

clue.text: He pays court to one appearing in court

definitions.meaning: a man who woos a woman
a litigant who brings a lawsuit

explanation.definitionFit: A wooer courts a woman; a petitioner brings a suit to law.

clue.text: Introduce males into corrupt shows

parts.note: to enter something is to introduce it, as an entry in a record

indicators.note: the males are put into the corrupt word, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to taint is to corrupt or spoil
men are males

explanation.surface: A complaint that letting men in has ruined the theatre programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Shows and performances provide amusement for an audience.
